_comment: Per-document invariant exemptions. An invariant listed here still RUNS, and its
failures are still counted and printed -- they just do not fail the build for the
one document named in `applies_to`. Everything else on the lane still gates.
`applies_to` is a substring of metadata.filename, the same scoping rule cases use.
`invariant` must name an entry in the lane's ALL_INVARIANTS (a test asserts this,
so a typo is a failure rather than a silently ineffective exemption).
Every entry below was traced to its source PDF before being written. The bar for
adding one is that the invariant is RIGHT and the document is genuinely outside
what the pipeline can read today -- never that a check is inconvenient. If an
exemption's invariant starts passing, the suite says so and the entry is deleted.

exemptions.reason: The source PDF's text layer emits the run as ONE 75-character token with no space glyphs inside it, so there is no positional information to split on. Recovering the spaces needs dictionary or language-model word splitting, which is non-deterministic and excluded by the README's 'no LLM/vision in the conversion path'.
Same cause as Customs Rules above: a single jammed token in the source PDF's text layer, no space glyphs to split on.
Same cause: jammed tokens in the source PDF's text layer, e.g. 'whetherthemonthlyreturnsfurnishedbytheregisteredpersoncorrectlyreflect' arrives from pdfplumber as one token.

The parser refuses this merge DELIBERATELY. Footnote 54.104 prints 'dated 21 st June, 2006'; pagemodel's discriminators for a raised suffix are a size drop and the absence of a space glyph, and this token is equal size (8.04pt), dtop 0.00, with a real space -- indistinguishable from a genuine '21 st' typo in the source. Merging it would merge real typos too. The invariant does not know the parser made that choice.
Same deliberate parser refusal as the 2005 edition above: an equal-size, space-separated ordinal suffix that cannot be told apart from a source typo.

Three heading-only leaves, each traced to a PRINTING ERROR in the source that hides the rule's own code from the body reader. The invariant is right: the body text really is in the preceding leaf. (1) Rule 44A, PDF page 66, prints a LEFT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK before the code -- '“44A. -Selection and conduct of audit.-(1) This rule shall apply to selection of cases for audit by the FBR' -- where its contents row on page 5 reads '44A. Selection and conduct of audit'. (2) Rule 150W, PDF page 109, DROPS THE LEADING DIGIT of its own code: the body prints '228[50W. Audit.-- The integrated supplier shall allow physical and online remote access' while the contents row on page 10 reads '150W. Audit'. (3) Rule 150ZQZI, PDF page 151, prints its code with a LOWERCASE L for the capital I -- '150ZQZl. Functions of the licensing committee.—' -- and page 152 carries a genuinely DIFFERENT rule, '150ZQZL. Right granted to the licensee', so the two cannot be folded together. Its contents row on page 13 also carries the printer's typo 'liceensing'. None of the three can be read without making the parser wrong about correct documents: admitting a left double quote as a code prefix, accepting a code whose digits do not match its contents row, or collapsing l->I, which would collide 150ZQZl with the real 150ZQZL. NO EXPIRY. All three are permanent defects in a 'native-digital' source (metadata source_kind), so none of them is an OCR artifact and none clears on the OCR decision -- correcting an earlier note in handover/tasks.md that called 150ZQZl OCR-class. These are the three hits this entry covers and they are enumerated on purpose: a FOURTH hit on this document would be a new defect this entry does not describe, and the reason should be re-read rather than assumed to cover it.
